findings.summary: Duplicate/dead test: 'queries real tables with rows' is defined twice with nearly identical setup, doing the same work twice and adding no new coverage
findings.evidence: Lines 114-197 add a new test named 'queries real tables with rows' that creates _test_products, inserts rows, and asserts via toCell(). Lines 309-391 contain a second, unmodified test with the exact same name and nearly identical body (same table name/inserts), asserting the pre-existing behavior directly with toEqual. This looks like a leftover from the diff that wasn't removed after the new version was added — it doubles the runtime of this scenario and doesn't add any distinct coverage; it also risks confusion about which version is the 'real' regression test for the new parser/toCell behavior.

findings.summary: The new toCell()-based formatting wired into ReadOnlyStore.loadQueryResults has no direct test exercising that integration point; only the standalone toCell() function is exercised (via the backend e2e suite), not the grid.set(...) call site that actually uses it in the sheets package
searchedFor: glob packages/sheets/**/*.test.ts (checked full list, no readonly/store test references ReadOnlyStore.loadQueryResults)
findings.evidence: readonly.ts line 73 changed `this.grid.set(sref, { v: String(val) })` to `this.grid.set(sref, { v: toCell(val) })` — a real behavior change (e.g. Date values now render as ISO strings instead of Date#toString() output, objects render as JSON instead of '[object Object]'). No test in packages/sheets exercises ReadOnlyStore.loadQueryResults with a Date or object value to confirm the grid cell actually receives the toCell-formatted string. The only coverage of toCell's Date/object branches is in the backend e2e suite, which calls toCell(...) directly on raw pg values — it never goes through ReadOnlyStore, so the actual wiring change in readonly.ts is unverified by any test in the repo.

findings.summary: Duplicate 'queries real tables with rows' test left in place after inserting a new, more thorough test of the same name and near-identical body
findings.evidence: The diff adds a new `it('queries real tables with rows', ...)` block (line 114 in the new file) that creates/queries/drops `_test_products`, but the pre-existing test with the exact same name and near-identical body (originally right after the block the diff inserted before) was left in the file unchanged at line 309-391. Both tests create the same table `_test_products`, insert the same rows, and assert on it — the second appears to be dead leftover from the change that should have replaced or removed it. This wastes CI time and, if PostgreSQL test isolation/teardown ever runs tests concurrently or one test's cleanup fails, could cause a real collision on the shared table name.

findings.summary: Mock in 'converts query runtime failures to bad request' test wasn't updated for the two new SET queries, so the simulated failure now fires at the SET TimeZone step instead of at the actual SELECT — test still passes but no longer exercises the intended failure path (query execution failure), only failure during session setup
findings.evidence: client.query.mockImplementation only special-cases `sql.startsWith('SET statement_timeout')`; the newly added `SET TimeZone = 'UTC'` and `SET DateStyle = 'ISO, MDY'` calls now hit the `else` branch and throw immediately, so the assertion no longer verifies a failure from the actual data query as originally intended.

findings.summary: datasourceTypeParser returns a plain identity function for DATE/TIMESTAMP/TIMESTAMPTZ regardless of the `format` argument. If pg ever negotiates binary format for these oids, the value passed would be a Buffer rather than a string and would be returned unchanged instead of decoded, silently corrupting the value. Currently unreachable since all queries here use the text simple-query protocol, but the guard does not explicitly exclude binary format.
findings.evidence: datasourceTypeParser = (oid, format) => RAW_TEXT_OIDS.has(oid) ? (value: string) => value : getDefaultParser(oid, format); — the RAW_TEXT_OIDS branch ignores `format`, so a binary-format value (a Buffer) would be returned as-is instead of parsed.

verdict.reason: The code the finding points to is real (RAW_TEXT_OIDS/datasourceTypeParser override in packages/backend/src/datasource/datasource.service.ts:19-37,144-145,204, and the toCell helper in packages/sheets/src/store/readonly.ts:29-36,73), but it is a targeted bug fix for value serialization, not an "architecture / data-model change." Per CONTRIBUTING.md:9-17 and 42-49, design-doc updates are required for "Feature / non-trivial change[s]" and "Architecture / data-model changes"; plain bug fixes go straight from issue → branch → PR with no design-doc obligation. This change only corrects how already-documented, already-limited behavior is serialized (dates shifted by server timezone, objects rendered as `[object Object]`) — it does not alter the document's model, the `ReadOnlyStore` contract, the API surface, or the multi-tab architecture described in docs/design/sheets/datasource.md. Critically, the doc's 'Current Limitations' #9 ("No column type mapping — All values are displayed as strings regardless of the PostgreSQL data type", datasource.md:205) and the Medium-term 'Column type awareness' goal (datasource.md:221) remain fully accurate after this change: values are still coerced to plain strings (`toCell` returns `string`), just with a bug fixed in how dates/objects stringify. The doc is therefore not made stale or inaccurate by this diff — the limitation it documents is preserved, not contradicted. This is a case where the referenced design doc doesn't need a line-item update for an internal serialization/bugfix detail; that is out of scope for the design-doc-discipline rubric, which targets architecture/data-model changes, not implementation bug fixes within an already-documented subsystem.

samples.summary: New e2e test expects CIRCLE and INTERVAL columns to be rendered as JSON objects (e.g. {x,y,radius} and {years,months,days}), but the production datasourceTypeParser only overrides DATE/TIMESTAMP/TIMESTAMPTZ; CIRCLE and INTERVAL fall through to pg's default type parser, which returns the raw postgres text representation, not a parsed object. There is a real mismatch between the asserted/intended behavior and what the shipped code actually produces for these types.
samples.evidence: RAW_TEXT_OIDS only contains DATE/TIMESTAMP/TIMESTAMPTZ (datasource.service.ts:21-25); no parser override exists for CIRCLE/INTERVAL, yet database.e2e-spec.ts (typeMap entries for CIRCLE and INTERVAL) assert toCell(rows[0].val) yields JSON-object-shaped strings for those types, which pg's default (unoverridden) text parser does not produce.

verdict.reason: The finding assumes pg's default (unoverridden) type parser returns raw postgres text for CIRCLE/INTERVAL. That premise is false. `datasourceTypeParser` (datasource.service.ts:34-37) only special-cases DATE/TIMESTAMP/TIMESTAMPTZ via RAW_TEXT_OIDS (lines 21-25) and for every other OID calls `getDefaultParser(oid, format)` — i.e. pg's own built-in type parser from the `pg-types` package. `pg-types` ships built-in smart parsers for CIRCLE (OID 718, parsed to `{x,y,radius}`) and INTERVAL (OID 1186, parsed via the `postgres-interval` package to `{years,months,days,...}` with only present fields populated) — this is long-standing, well-documented default behavior of node-postgres, not something the app needs to add. The lockfile confirms the dependency chain is present: `pnpm-lock.yaml:15396-15402` shows `pg-types@2.2.0` depending on `postgres-interval@1.2.0`, `postgres-array@2.0.0`, and `postgres-date@1.0.7` — the exact machinery that performs this default object-shaped parsing. So the fallthrough to `getDefaultParser` for CIRCLE/INTERVAL (datasource.service.ts:35-37) is precisely what produces the JSON-object-shaped values the e2e test (database.e2e-spec.ts:242,254) asserts, once passed through `toCell`'s `typeof val === 'object' -> JSON.stringify` branch (packages/sheets/src/store/readonly.ts:32-36). There is no mismatch between the test's expectations and the shipped code; no override is missing because the default already does the job.
